title: Wych Elm 'Exoniensis': Ancient Feather Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: A narrow, upright wych elm cultivar the Dutch call the feather elm. All three the site maps stand in Leeuwarden, one wearing a five-metre graft scar.
intro: This is the feather elm, pluimiep in Dutch, a cultivar of wych elm bred narrow and upright where the wild species spreads wide, and grafted about 1.5 metres up the trunk to keep that shape. Old wych elms of any kind are a rare sight after a century of Dutch elm disease took most of them out, which is reason enough to go looking for the three this site maps, all of them, by coincidence of where the registers have looked, standing in Leeuwarden. Two grow in the small Vosseparkje at the edge of the old town, a short walk apart and told apart mainly by which one stands nearer the pond. The third is a street planting on Molenstraat, where the graft union on the larger of the pair has swollen into a scar tissue collar over five metres round, wider at that one point than the trunk beneath it, with a fern rooted in its canopy. None of the three has a written history beyond the national monument register. What they have is a shape nobody plants any more and a graft nobody has fully explained.
